Every call

The board's call and odds: the board's model judging each call on what was known when it was made. Confidence: across the simulated weeks, each weighted by how much the choice changed it (a matchup or median flip counts 1), the share of the difference that went the board's way (Toss-up under 55%, Lean 55-65%, Likely 65-80%, Clear 80%+). Verdicts go by real results first: the matchup and the median with the team's call against the same week with the other call (Same result when both give the same wins); points are shown under them. A lock is judged against what not locking would really have ended with: the board's own plan for that slot played out (week 4 on), or his later games kept when they cleared the board's line (weeks 1-3); a score left unlocked against what the slot ended with. Before lineup tracking (weeks 1-3, before the Mac logged lineups): the lock records show the score wasn't locked, but not whether he was in the lineup then. Updated Nov 24, 9:19 PM.
